in_arabic.name: أبراهيم
in_arabic.meaning: أبو الرحمة، أبي الإيمان، أخ النبي إسماعيل
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه أبو الرحمة، أبي الإيمان، أخ النبي إسماعيل، ويعتبر إبراهيم عليه السلام من أعظم الأنبياء في الإسلام، وقد ورد ذكره في القرآن الكريم في عدة سور، وهو رمز للإيمان والتوحيد.

in_urdu.name: ابراہیم
in_urdu.meaning: رحمت کا باپ، ایمان کا باپ، حضرت اسماعیل کا بھائی
in_urdu.long_meaning: ابراہیم نام علم کا ایک مذکر نام ہے جو عربی मूल سے ہے، اور اس کا مطلب رحمت کا باپ، ایمان کا باپ، حضرت اسماعیل کا بھائی ہوتا ہے۔ اسلامی تقویم میں، ابراہیم علیہ السلام ایک عظیم نبی مانے جاتے ہیں، اور ان کا ذکر قرآن کریم میں کئی سورتوں میں کیا گیا ہے۔ یہ نام ایمان، توحید اور روحانی رہنمائی کی علامت ہے۔

data.cultural_impact: The name Abrahim hold deep cultural significance in both the Islamic and Jewish traditions. Abrahim is considered to be a pivotal figure in the history of monotheism, as he is believed to be the founder and the first representative of the monotheistic faiths. In Islam, Abrahim is revered as a prophet and a essential figure in the religious history of the Islamic community. The early Muslims regarded Abrahim as an divine figure whose unique bond with God paved the way for the development of the Islamic faith. Additionally, many Islamic and Jewish traditions emphasize on Abrahim's unwavering faith, obedience, and belief in the One God. His actions, sacrifices, and beliefs have left a lasting impact on the cultural fabric of both the Islamic and Jewish communities.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Abrahim holds profound spiritual significance as it is considered to be a symbol of faith, obedience, and unwavering commitment to God. In the Islamic tradition, Abrahim is believed to have received God's command to leave his homeland and migrate to a land that he would be shown. He was willing to sacrifice his wife, his son, and all his worldly possessions in obedience to God's command. This unwavering faith, obedience, and trust in God's divine plan inspired countless generations of followers. The spiritual significance of the name Abrahim is not limited to the Islamic community, but it is also profoundly meaningful in the Jewish tradition. Abrahim is considered to be the patriarch of the Jewish people, and his faith and obedience to God serve as an essential reminder of the importance of maintaining a close relationship with God and upholding the Ten Commandments. The spiritual significance of the name Abrahim is a powerful reminder of the importance of maintaining faith, obedience, and trust in God, regardless of the challenges and hardships of life.
